proposed_reports.title: Financial Information Return (FIR) Instructions and Introduction
proposed_reports.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing
proposed_reports.description: The official annual instruction set and introduction for completing the Ontario Financial Information Return. Explicitly states that FIR data must reflect the municipality’s audited financial statements prepared under PSAB standards, details every schedule (taxation, operations, debt, development charges, etc.), and announces the 2027 template rewrite to implement the new PS 1202 reporting model.

proposed_reports.title: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting in the Public Sector
proposed_reports.publisher: Public Sector Accounting Board (PSAB) / CPA Canada
proposed_reports.description: The revised conceptual framework issued by PSAB in December 2022 that replaces the prior PS 1000 / PS 1100 concepts. It underpins all public-sector accounting standards in Canada and is the foundation for the new financial-statement presentation model (PS 1202). Effective for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 April 2026.

proposed_reports.title: PS 1202 Financial Statement Presentation (New Reporting Model)
proposed_reports.publisher: Public Sector Accounting Board (PSAB) / CPA Canada
proposed_reports.description: The new financial-statement presentation standard that replaces PS 1201. Requires a revised set of statements (financial position, net financial assets/liabilities, operations, changes in net assets/liabilities, cash flow) and is the concrete expression of the revised Conceptual Framework. Effective for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 April 2026; Ontario has confirmed the 2027 FIR will be rewritten to match it.

dependencies.basis: The official FIR Introduction states that the information in the Return must reflect the audited financial statements of the municipality prepared under PSAB standards.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The information included in the Financial Information Return should reflect the audited financial statements of the municipality (PSAB Standards).

dependencies.basis: The FIR Instructions and Introduction repeatedly require municipalities to follow the same PSAB Handbook standards used for their audited financial statements (tangible capital assets PS 3150, government reporting entity PS 1300, asset retirement obligations PS 3280, etc.).
dependencies.evidence_quote: Please follow the same accounting and financial reporting standards contained in the PSA Handbook: PS 3150 Tangible Capital Assets that are utilized to produce the annual financial statements.

dependencies.basis: Municipalities complete the FIR using the official annual Instructions and Introduction issued by the Ministry; the template itself contains over 1 400 verification checks derived from those instructions.
dependencies.evidence_quote: To further assist municipalities with completing the FIR, over 1400 data verification checks are built into the template.

dependencies.basis: The Ministry has publicly announced that the 2027 FIR template will be updated to reflect the new PSAB standard PS 1202 Financial Statement Presentation that implements the revised Conceptual Framework.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing is updating the 2027 FIR to reflect the new Public Sector Accounting Board (PSAB) standard PS 1202 Financial Statement Presentation. Based on the revised Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting in the Public Sector, PS 1202 sets out general and specific requirements for the presentation of [financial statements].

dependencies.basis: PS 1202 is the concrete reporting-model standard that implements the concepts set out in the revised Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting in the Public Sector; the two are adopted together.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Both the Conceptual Framework and the Reporting Model in Section PS 1202 will be effective for fiscal years beginning on or after April 1, 2026. Earlier adoption is permitted only if the Conceptual Framework is also adopted at the same time.

dependencies.basis: City of Toronto audited consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards established by the Public Sector Accounting Board.
dependencies.evidence_quote: All City financial statements are prepared in accordance with Public Sector Accounting Standards (PSAS) established by the Public Sector Accounting Board (PSAB) of the Chartered Professional Accountants (CPA) of Canada.

dependencies.basis: City of Ottawa audited consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards established by the Public Sector Accounting Board, as required by the Municipal Act.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The City of Ottawa Annual Financial Reports contain the audited consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards established by the Public Sector Accounting Board [‘PSAB’] of the Chartered Professional Accountants of Canada [“CPA Canada”], as required by the Ontario Municipal Act.

dependencies.basis: The FIR is a standardized extraction of data drawn from each municipality’s audited financial statements. Toronto’s Consolidated Financial Statements are the source for its FIR submission.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Through the FIR template ... the Ministry collects data on municipal financial position and activities ... based on the audited financial statements.

dependencies.basis: Already established in the prior Ontario slice; the OMPF Technical Guide Appendix F names the Municipal FIR as the source for PIL Weighted Assessment. The present batch simply re-confirms the data-flow direction from the municipal audited statements through the FIR into the provincial transfer formula.
